basics.name: Seokha Moon
basics.label: AI Planning Researcher @ KakaoMobility | Ph.D. | Autonomous Driving 🚗 & Robotics 🤖
basics.summary: I completed my Ph.D. at Korea University's Vision & AI Lab, advised by Prof. Jungbeom Lee and Prof. Jinkyu Kim, and currently work as an AI planning researcher in KakaoMobility's Autonomous Driving Development Team. My research focuses on autonomous driving and robotics across perception, prediction, and planning. I have led first-author projects on multi-camera 3D object detection, streaming 3D occupancy prediction, VLM-guided trajectory prediction, and end-to-end planning. My current interests include reliable closed-loop planning and Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models that connect perception, reasoning, and decision-making.

education.studyType: Ph.D. (Advisors: Prof. Jungbeom Lee and Prof. Jinkyu Kim)

work.name: KakaoMobility
work.position: Planner Developer – Autonomous Driving Development Team
work.summary: Developing planning algorithms for real-vehicle autonomous driving.
highlights: Developing planning algorithms that transform perception, prediction, map, and vehicle-state inputs into safe and natural autonomous driving behavior and trajectories.
Analyzing scenario-level failures and improving behavior decision, trajectory generation, real-time integration, and verification logic for real-vehicle deployment.

work.name: NAVER LABS
work.summary: Led a streaming 3D occupancy prediction project for camera-based 3D scene understanding (StreamOcc, ECCV 2026).
highlights: Defined the latency, memory, and coordinate-alignment issues in multi-frame fusion.
Designed stream-based voxel aggregation and query-guided refinement to preserve dense spatial representations while improving real-time efficiency and dynamic-object modeling.

work.name: 42dot
work.summary: Developed interaction-aware trajectory prediction models for multi-agent intersection scenarios.
highlights: Designed a future-aware teacher-student distillation framework that transfers interaction knowledge from privileged future observations to an efficient inference-time model.
Published at ICPR 2024 and the CVPR 2023 Workshop on Vision-Centric Autonomous Driving.

work.name: Korea Univ. Vision & AI Lab
work.summary: Worked on multi-camera 3D object detection and occupancy prediction.
highlights: Worked on ORA3D and Waymo occupancy-challenge baselines.
Built perception data processing and evaluation pipelines for 3D detection and occupancy prediction experiments.

work.name: Samsung Electronics
work.summary: Implemented an attention-based few-shot face detection algorithm for limited-data settings.
highlights: Built and curated a face dataset and designed augmentation pipelines covering scale, crop, color, and blur variations.
